articles.title: RSI Arena: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement with Human Feedback
articles.summary: The paper introduces RSI Arena, a two-stage experiment testing whether frontier AI agents can autonomously post-train language models and improve them using human feedback. Ten agents trained models from NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B Base using limited compute and API budgets, with all producing working assistants and the best model closing 76% of the base-to-Instruct benchmark gap. A second stage using human comparison feedback improved style-adjusted preference ratings for most models, though benchmark gains were modest and one model showed higher harmful compliance.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is early-stage research rather than a commercial deployment, but it is relevant because it points toward AI systems that can increasingly manage parts of the model-development workflow themselves. If such approaches mature, they could affect demand for compute infrastructure, model governance tools, and AI safety evaluation, while potentially lowering some labor bottlenecks in model post-training.

articles.title: GENCO - A Unified Neural Solver Embedded in a Development Framework for Steady-State Grid Analysis
articles.original_publisher: A Unified Neural Solver Embedded in a Development Framework for Steady-State Grid Analysis
articles.summary: GENCO is presented as a unified neural solver for steady-state transmission grid analysis, covering power flow, optimal power flow, and state estimation within one architecture. The authors also introduce an open-source GridFM Development Framework and large-scale datasets, with evaluations showing significant speedups versus classical solvers and testing on real-world Hydro-Québec SCADA data.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is an early but relevant example of AI moving into engineering-heavy utility workflows where accuracy, feasibility, and physical constraints matter. If approaches like this mature, they could support faster grid planning and operations, with potential long-term implications for utilities, grid software providers, and infrastructure modernization beneficiaries.
